title: Countable hypercohomology with a perfect factor
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], with schemes [def-pc-scheme], algebraic spaces with their small etale structure sheaves [def-trf-algebraic-space], module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and unbounded derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Write $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ for objects with quasi-coherent cohomology [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Perfect means etale locally represented by a bounded complex of direct summands of finite free structure modules [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package]. A space is quasi-compact if its point space is quasi-compact and quasi-separated if its absolute diagonal is quasi-compact on scheme tests. Let $S$ be a scheme, let $X$ be a quasi-compact quasi-separated algebraic space over $S$, and let $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$. Assume that $\mathcal H^i(K)(V)$ is a countable set for every integer $i$ and every affine scheme $V$ etale over $X$. For every quasi-compact quasi-separated etale morphism $v:U\to X$, every perfect $P\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ and every integer $i$, the underlying set of $H^iR\Gamma(U,v^*(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_X}P))$ is countable. Here restriction along an etale map is exact, tensor is computed with K-flat resolutions, and derived sections with K-injective resolutions; $R\Gamma$ is the derived module global-section functor [def-pur-ringed-site-zeroth-hypercohomology]. No boundedness hypothesis on $K$ is imposed.

proof.text: Fix $K$ and a perfect $P$ as in the statement. For a qcqs etale space $t:T\to X$ let $C(T)$ mean that $H^nR\Gamma(T,t^*(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}P))$ is countable for every integer $n$. By [lem-sfb-space-derived-etale-chart-calculus], restriction is exact, preserves quasi-coherent cohomology and composes canonically. By [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] it identifies this restricted tensor with $t^*K\otimes^{\mathbf L}t^*P$. The local finite-free splittings defining perfectness restrict to the pulled-back etale cover, so $t^*P$ is perfect. Exact restriction also identifies $\mathcal H^j(t^*K)$ with $t^*\mathcal H^j(K)$. On an affine etale $T\to X$ its global sections are therefore countable by hypothesis. Apply [lem-sfb-affine-countable-perfect-tensor] to $L=t^*K$ and $Q=t^*P$. This proves the affine base case $C(T)$, including the empty affine.

source.place: Tag 0CRU, affine base case; Tag 0CRP, affine proof paragraph

proof.text: Consider an elementary distinguished square $(A\subset W,B\to W)$ of qcqs etale objects over $X$ in the induction theorem, and put $D=A\times_WB$ and $F=(K\otimes^{\mathbf L}P)|_W$. Apply [lem-sfb-space-derived-hom-mayer-vietoris] with first argument $\mathcal O_W$ in degree zero and second argument $F$. The additive bijections of [lem-sfb-ringed-hypercohomology-shifted-unit], with base ring $\mathbf Z$, identify $\operatorname{Ext}^n(\mathcal O_Z,F|_Z)$ with $H^nR\Gamma(Z,F|_Z)$ for $Z=W,A,B,D$: shift the degree-zero unit into degree $n$ in the source of Hom. Thus the sequence gives an exact segment $H^{n-1}R\Gamma(D,F|_D)\to H^nR\Gamma(W,F)\to H^nR\Gamma(A,F|_A)\oplus H^nR\Gamma(B,F|_B)$. All these restrictions are the ones in $C$ by exact etale restriction and its composition comparison from step 1. Neither cited theorem imposes a boundedness condition on $F$.

source.place: Tag 0CRU, distinguished-square step; Tag 0CRS (lemma-unbounded-mayer-vietoris), exact sequence, obtained here from existing derived-Hom Mayer–Vietoris

proof.text: Assume $C(A),C(B),C(D)$. In the exact segment of step 2 write $G=H^nR\Gamma(W,F)$. The kernel of the map from $G$ to the countable finite direct sum is the image of a countable group, hence countable. Its quotient in $G$ embeds into that finite direct sum, so it too is countable. Choose one representative of each quotient class; addition gives a surjection from the product of the countable kernel and this countable set of representatives onto $G$. A product of two countable sets is countable, so $G$ is countable. This holds for every $n$, proving $C(W)$. Apply [lem-sfb-space-qcqs-distinguished-square-induction] with the property $C$: step 1 supplies all affine objects and this argument supplies precisely the required gluing implication. Consequently $C$ holds for every qcqs etale space over $X$.

source.place: Tag 0CRU, final paragraph; Tag 08GP (lemma-induction-principle), hypotheses (1) and (2)

proof.text: For the morphism $v:U\to X$ in the statement we show that $U$ is qcqs. First, for any algebraic space $Z$ over $S$, $|Z|$ is quasi-compact exactly when $Z$ admits a representable surjective etale map from a quasi-compact scheme: one direction is [lem-sfb-qc-space-affine-etale-atlas], which even gives an affine atlas. Conversely, for a representable surjective etale $a:h_W\to Z$ the map $|a|$ is continuous by the definition of the atlas topology [def-a1-space-point-topology], and surjective: for a field point $\operatorname{Spec}K\to Z$ the scheme $W\times_Z\operatorname{Spec}K$ maps onto $\operatorname{Spec}K$, so it is nonempty, and any of its points gives a $W$-point over a field extension of $K$ in the same class. Hence $|Z|$ is a continuous image of the quasi-compact space $|W|$, so it is quasi-compact. By the same image argument applied to atlases of the test spaces, a morphism is quasi-compact on scheme tests exactly when it is so on quasi-compact algebraic-space tests, and these may be taken affine [lem-sfb-space-quasicompact-affine-tests]; so all quasi-compactness notions used here agree. Now $X$ is quasi-compact, so testing the quasi-compact morphism $v$ on $X\xrightarrow{\mathrm{id}}X$ shows that $U=U\times_XX$ is quasi-compact. View the spaces over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$: the change-of-base equivalence [lem-sfb-space-change-base-to-integers] keeps their etale scheme charts and fibre products, hence their point spaces and diagonals. Then [lem-sfb-space-qcqs-source-products] gives quasi-separatedness of $U$ from that of $v$ and $X$. Therefore $U\to X$ is in the domain of $C$, and step 3 gives exactly the asserted countability for every integer $i$. No truncation or boundedness of $K$ was used.
